title: An 8.62μW 75dB-DR SoC End-to-End Spoken-Language-Understanding SoC With Channel-Level AGC and Temporal-Sparsity-Aware Streaming-Mode RNN
problem: Voice-controlled IoT and wearable devices require ultra-low-power always-on audio classification for continuous speech input (not just single-word) with >60dB input range to handle variable speech volume. Prior designs either used costly analog front-ends (>50% of power) or analog feature extractors that couldn't achieve both low power and high accuracy on multi-class tasks with variable input levels.
motivation: Real-time spoken language understanding on resource-constrained edge devices demands aggressive power optimization in the analog front-end and feature extraction pipeline to enable persistent voice interfaces without external classifiers.
method: The chip combines automatic gain control (AGC — circuitry that automatically adjusts microphone sensitivity to handle different speech volumes) on each audio channel to process inputs ranging from quiet whispers to loud speech (>60dB range). A neural network processes the audio sequentially, recognizing that speech contains significant silence and repetition — it skips unnecessary analysis moments, reducing power consumption. The entire pipeline, from audio front-end to language recognition, runs on a single chip.
key_novelty: A neural network that saves power by exploiting natural pauses and repetition in speech, enabling end-to-end voice recognition on a single ultra-low-power chip with integrated audio level adjustment.
contributions: Ultra-low-power SoC achieving 8.62μW total power for full SLU pipeline
Channel-level AGC integrated on-chip to handle >60dB speech dynamic range without costly off-chip processing
Temporal-sparsity-aware streaming RNN that reduces computation vs. standard RNNs
End-to-end continuous speech understanding (not limited to keyword spotting or single-word inputs)
limitations: Not discussed—abstract does not specify KWS accuracy, latency, or exact number of SLU classes achieved.
primary_theme: Ultra-low-power SoC for always-on speech understanding
